Buying a few high-value Crypto cards (cost 6+) by Cycle 5 builds the economy that wins the late game.
Characters that draw cards cycle the deck back to its best cards faster than extra Crypto does.

notes.text: Founding guidance from the designer: gain a few high-value Crypto and Base cards first, then collect Chaos cards for an endgame play. Every game is different, so adapt to the market and the opponent.

Pre-launch self-play (80 headless games per profile vs scripted opponents): most games ended by Server destruction around Cycles 8-11. Valuing Drain early and pivoting to Chaos by Cycle 5 won 88-92% vs 71% for a Cycle 9 pivot. Extra Crypto lowered the win rate (70 -> 62 of 80 as the Crypto weight rose), because draw/Power Base cards return more per Crypto spent. Shyte-Coin is never bought. Human opponents deploy far better than the scripts, so re-test all of this against the human.

Prioritize acquiring Base cards with draw and Action effects to enhance early game efficiency.
Avoid Shyte-Coin; its low value dilutes deck quality.
Transition into Chaos around Cycle 5, as Drain becomes crucial for server destruction.
Plan to buy VP cards primarily in the late game to avoid clogging the hand too early.
Monitor the effectiveness of new cards for potential inclusion in strategy.

Cycle 2: Human opponent opted for Kilo-Coin; I maintained focus on draw and Chaos cards.

High-value Crypto is still a priority but should not dilute the deck with low-value cards.

Debrief: The human won at Cycle 11 (Both Servers destroyed. You win, 35 to 3 VP.). VP human 35 / me 3. Servers human 2249 / me 0. Human bought: Infernal Kernel x2, Mega-Cache x2, Sudo Demiurge, Byte-Coin, Superpositioning, Iterative Incubus, ∆-Wave, Temporal Rift, Root Rune, BIOS Archive, Zenith Wetware. I bought: Razor Blade Jade x2, Rezz Razor, Timed Bomb, Slash-Dot, Bumpster.

Theory evidence: no-shyte contradicted (Shyte-Coins owned: winner 1, loser 0); economy-first supported (Kilo/Mega Crypto bought by Cycle 5: winner 1, loser 0); draw-engine contradicted (cards of draw bought: winner 5, loser 6); chaos-endgame contradicted (Chaos bought from Cycle 8: winner 0, loser 1); drain-race supported (Servers destroyed at Cycle 11).
Adjusting: my Servers fell low, so Restore is worth more; the human won on VP bought earlier than my VP window; my mid-game Draft wallet averaged 1.5 vs the human's 9.8, so the Crypto target rises.
Human opponent effectively utilized high-value Crypto and Drain cards early, leading to significant Server damage.
I struggled with low Power early on; focusing on draw and Actions is critical.
The human's mid-game Draft wallet consistently outpaced mine, indicating a need for improved economic strategies.
Transitioning to Chaos by Cycle 5 was beneficial, but I need to buy more effective Chaos cards sooner.
Restore cards may need to be prioritized to mitigate Server damage.
The human's VP acquisition strategy was effective; I need to adjust my timing for VP purchases.

history.plan: Focus on acquiring strong draw/Action Base cards early to build an efficient economy. Avoid Shyte-Coin; prioritize high-value Crypto only when beneficial. Transition into Chaos by Cycle 5 to enhance Drain capabilities, aiming for a late-game push with VP cards post-Cycle 12. (Schedule: economy through Cycle 5, Chaos from Cycle 6, VP from Cycle 12.)

Acquire strong draw/Action Base cards early, prioritizing cards like Dash and Slash-Dot for efficiency. Avoid Shyte-Coin; focus on high-value Crypto when beneficial. Transition into Chaos by Cycle 5 to enhance Drain capabilities, utilizing cards like Bloodlet Drone and Rezz-Blade. Aim for a late-game push with VP cards after Cycle 12, leveraging the power from Drain to destroy Servers for VP. (Schedule: economy through Cycle 5, Chaos from Cycle 6, VP from Cycle 12.)
